$comment: Machine-readable preprocessing spec for the TypeScript/browser port (PR 3). Human-readable companion: docs/PREPROCESSING.md. Python reference implementation: extract_landmarks.py (landmark extraction, frame sampling) + transforms.py (normalize_body, mirror_clip). Golden test vectors generated against this spec by scripts/generate_golden_vectors.py.

model.note: num_classes and the dense-index <-> original-class-id mapping come from that checkpoint's label_map.json, not from this spec -- they depend on which classes were in the training data, not on the preprocessing steps below.

groups.name: left_hand
groups.source: MediaPipe Hand landmarks, in MediaPipe's own landmark order (0 = wrist)

groups.name: right_hand
groups.source: MediaPipe Hand landmarks, in MediaPipe's own landmark order (0 = wrist)

landmark_layout.coordinate_units: MediaPipe's own normalized landmark coordinates: x, y in [0, 1] relative to the input frame's width/height; z roughly on the same scale, relative depth (MediaPipe's own convention, hip-depth-relative for Pose/Holistic) -- NOT re-normalized to a fixed physical unit before normalize_body is applied.

frame_sampling.method: evenly spaced sample indices across the whole clip, from the first to the last frame inclusive
frame_sampling.formula: index[i] = floor( i * (total_frames - 1) / (sequence_length - 1) )  for i = 0 .. sequence_length - 1
frame_sampling.rounding: truncate toward zero (NOT round-to-nearest). Verified against numpy: np.linspace(0, total_frames - 1, sequence_length, dtype=int) truncates the float linspace result, e.g. np.linspace(0, 2, 5, dtype=int) == [0, 0, 1, 1, 2], not [0, 1, 1, 2, 2].
frame_sampling.edge_case_total_frames_le_0: if total_frames <= 0, sample list is empty (extract_landmarks.py returns an all-zero/all-missing clip in this case; shouldn't occur for a real recorded clip).

mask_semantics.meaning: 1 = this joint was detected by MediaPipe in this sampled frame; 0 = not detected (and that joint's x/y/z are written as exactly 0.0 in the raw landmarks array for that frame -- the mask is what distinguishes 'detected at the origin' from 'not detected', not the coordinate value itself).
mask_semantics.granularity: left_hand and right_hand are each set as a whole 21-joint block per frame (MediaPipe's hand detector either finds a whole hand or it doesn't -- there's no partial-hand detection in this pipeline). The 5 pose joints are likewise all set together per frame, since they all come from the same single pose-detection result.

normalize_body.applied: always, as part of the production recipe (config f) -- deterministic, not random, applied identically to every clip (train/val/test/inference), BEFORE any augmentation/TTA step below.
normalize_body.reference_frames: only frames where BOTH left_shoulder (index 43) and right_shoulder (index 44) are detected (mask == 1 for both) contribute to the two statistics below. If NO frame in the clip has both shoulders detected, normalize_body is a no-op (the clip's raw landmarks pass through unchanged) -- there's no body frame to normalize into.

mid_shoulder_point.definition: mean, over reference frames only, of ((left_shoulder_xyz + right_shoulder_xyz) / 2) -- a single (x, y, z) 3-vector for the whole clip, not per-frame.
mid_shoulder_point.applied_as: subtracted from every joint's (x, y, z) in every frame of the clip (not just reference frames).

shoulder_width.definition: mean, over reference frames only, of the 3D Euclidean distance between left_shoulder and right_shoulder in that frame -- a single scalar for the whole clip.
shoulder_width.applied_as: every joint's (x, y, z), after subtracting mid_shoulder_point, is divided by this scalar (all three axes divided by the same scalar -- this is NOT independently normalizing x, y, z ranges).
shoulder_width.epsilon_guard: max(shoulder_width, 1e-6) -- guards against division by (near-)zero if the clip's shoulders are degenerate.

normalize_body.missing_joint_handling: after normalizing, any (frame, joint) with mask == 0 is forced to exactly (0.0, 0.0, 0.0) -- NOT left at '-mid_shoulder_point / shoulder_width' (which would make a missing joint look like a detected joint sitting exactly at the body center). The mask itself is unchanged by normalize_body.

mirror_tta.when_used: inference-time test-time augmentation only (the production recipe's --tta-mirror). NOT used during training data augmentation in the exported model's forward pass -- mirror-aug at train time uses the identical transform but is a stochastic (p=0.5 per sample) training augmentation, not something the browser needs to implement at all for inference.
mirror_tta.order_relative_to_normalize_body: mirroring is applied AFTER normalize_body, to the already-normalized coordinates -- not to the raw landmarks.

transform.reflect_axis: x only (y and z are left unchanged)

reflect_point_per_frame.primary: if both shoulders (indices 43, 44) are detected in this frame: (left_shoulder_x + right_shoulder_x) / 2, computed for that frame alone.
reflect_point_per_frame.fallback_1: if not: the clip's mean of that same per-frame value, averaged over whichever frames in the clip DO have both shoulders detected.
reflect_point_per_frame.fallback_2: if NO frame in the clip has both shoulders detected: 0.5 (reflect about the frame's own horizontal center -- a least-assumption fallback; note this is in NORMALIZED-BODY coordinate space at this point, not raw [0,1] pixel space, since mirroring happens after normalize_body).

transform.reflection_formula: mirrored_x = 2 * reflect_point_x - original_x, applied per-frame using that frame's own reflect_point_x from the fallback chain above.

slot_swaps_after_reflecting.note: whole 21-joint blocks, coordinates AND mask both swapped together

unchanged: nose (42) -- a single joint, not paired, so it only gets reflected in x, never swapped with anything
mirror_tta.idempotent: mirroring twice returns the exact original clip (verified in test_transforms.py) -- useful as a self-check when porting.

inference_combination.rule: run the model on BOTH the normalized original input AND the normalized+mirrored input, take softmax of each output separately, then AVERAGE THE TWO SOFTMAX PROBABILITY VECTORS (not the raw logits) -- then argmax/top-k on that averaged probability vector.
inference_combination.why_softmax_not_logits: averaging raw logits from two different forward passes has no principled interpretation as a combined confidence; averaging probabilities does (it's the mixture-of-two-views prediction).

mirror_tta.python_reference: transforms.mirror_clip() for the transform; evaluate.py's evaluate_split(tta_mirror=True) for the inference-time combination.

not_part_of_production_recipe.trim_idle: implemented in transforms.py and available via train.py/evaluate.py's --trim-idle flag, but explicitly dropped from the production recipe (config f) -- see RESULTS.md's Decisions section (no measured gain, made one diagnosed-outlier signer worse, extra complexity with no payoff). The browser/PR 3 does NOT need to implement idle-frame trimming.
